In quale direzione si legge una parola a: In which direction do you read an Arabic word?
Le parole arabe si leggono da destra a s: Arabic words are read from right to left. The letters within them follow the same direction.
Quale lettera ha due punti sopra?: Which letter has two dots above it?
ب è bāʾ: ha un punto sotto. ت ha due pun: ب is bāʾ: it has one dot below. ت has two dots above; ن has one dot above.
ت è tāʾ, il suono /t/. I due punti sopra: ت is tāʾ, the /t/ sound. Its two dots above distinguish it from ب and ث.
ث è ṯāʾ, /θ/: la lingua si avvicina ai d: ث is ṯāʾ, /θ/: bring your tongue close to your upper teeth and let air pass through. It is not pronounced like ت.
Quale vocale breve indica la fatḥa َ ?: Which short vowel does fatḥa َ represent?
La fatḥa َ indica a breve; la kasra ِ in: Fatḥa َ represents short a; kasra ِ represents i; ḍamma ُ represents u.
La kasra sotto ب indica i breve: بِ si l: The kasra below ب represents short i: بِ is read bi.
Una consonante senza vocale breve: A consonant without a short vowel
Il sukūn indica assenza di vocale breve: Sukūn indicates that no short vowel follows the consonant. Šadda ّ indicates consonant doubling instead.
Componi bāb, «porta», scegliendo le lett: Build bāb, “door”, by choosing the letters in writing order (from right to left).
ب + ا + ب formano باب. La alif indica ā: ب + ا + ب form باب. Alif represents long ā and does not connect to the following letter: the final ب stays separate.
Scrivi in arabo bint («ragazza»), con la: Write bint (“girl”) in Arabic, including kasra and sukūn.
بِ si legge bi; نْ non ha vocale; ت chiu: بِ is read bi; نْ has no vowel; ت ends the word in its pausal form. Kasra and sukūn are part of the answer in this exercise.
باب significa «porta». Nei libri può anc: باب means “door”. In books it can also mean “chapter”. “Girl” is بنت; “straw” is تبن.

In questa prima unità impari a riconosce: In this first unit you will learn to recognise ا، ب، ت، ث، ن, distinguish their dots and build your first words. You do not need to memorise everything at once: read a step, try the exercises and revisit anything you find difficult.
Stai studiando arabo standard moderno (M: You are studying Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), the variety used in formal writing, documents and news broadcasts. Dialects will be covered separately.

Con questa unità passi dal leggere al co: In this unit, you move from reading to communicating. You will learn the expressions Arabic speakers use to greet each other, introduce themselves and say goodbye in Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), as well as the difference between addressing a man and a woman, which you can hear in every question in Arabic. These are fixed expressions: learn them as complete chunks. You will explore the grammar behind them in later units.
Radice e schema: come funziona la morfol: Roots and patterns: how Arabic morphology works
In A1 hai visto che ⁧كِتَاب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَب⁩: In A1, you saw that ⁧كِتَاب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَبَة⁩ and ⁧يَكْتُبُ⁩ share the same three consonants. In this unit, that observation becomes a practical tool: the root ( ⁧الجِذْر⁩ ) carries a general idea, while the pattern ( ⁧الوَزْن⁩ ) turns it into a verb, a person, a place or an action. With around twenty common patterns, you can understand words you have never studied and find them in a dictionary. For anyone reading Arabic sources, this is the most useful skill at this level. Two weeks.
Il livello B1 comincia con lo strumento: Level B1 begins with a tool you will use throughout the rest of the course: a dictionary organised by root. In A2, you learnt that almost every Arabic word comes from a root and a pattern (A2-01), and you recognised the derived forms (A2-18). Now you will turn that knowledge into a method: when you encounter an unfamiliar word, even without vowel marks, you will break it down layer by layer, identify its root even if a letter has disappeared or changed, find it in the dictionary and choose the meaning that fits the context. This step will help you work independently with the authentic texts in module B1.3. Two weeks.
Metodo di lettura autonoma di un articol: A method for reading articles independently
Il livello B2 comincia con un cambio di: Level B2 begins with a change of pace: from now on, you will read articles written in the style of pan-Arab newspapers, 300–400 words long, without vowel marks or simplified texts. The dictionary remains useful, but its role changes: it becomes your last resort, rather than your starting point. In this unit, you will learn a four-stage method (before reading, reading for gist, detailed reading and after reading), recognise genres in the Arabic press, locate the main verb in a long sentence, decide which words to look up, and use the framing expressions that connect a news item to its context ( ⁧عَلَى خَلْفِيَّةِ⁩ …, ⁧فِي إِطَارِ⁩ …, ⁧فِي ظِلِّ⁩ …). Three weeks, alongside EGY-11.
Diplomazia: vertici, comunicati, dichiar: Diplomacy: summits, communiqués and joint statements
La diplomazia parla una lingua codificat: Diplomacy uses a coded language. A ‘frank’ meeting is one in which the parties disagree; ‘agreeing to continue consultations’ often means that no agreement has been reached; and ‘expresses concern’, ‘condemns’ and ‘strongly condemns’ sit at distinct points on a scale. Anyone reading open sources needs to understand this code without exaggerating or overlooking its nuances. In this unit, you will learn the vocabulary of visits and summits, the ‘thermometer’ of diplomatic adjectives, the scale of verbs used in communiqués and resolutions, the structure of a joint statement (including clauses introduced by ⁧إِذْ⁩ ), diplomatic actions (summoning an ambassador, recalling one, severing relations) and how to read what a communiqué leaves unsaid. The sources in the texts are fictional; the writing exercise uses a real public communiqué. Two weeks.
